turns.question: Our project concerns scaling stateful workers while preserving stable resource names. For the planned deployment, set application.id to oak-scale-17. Which value should we use, and which ordering of processing and offset saving gives at-least-once consumption?
turns.standalone_question: For this Kafka project, our project concerns scaling stateful workers while preserving stable resource names. For the planned deployment, set application.id to oak-scale-17. Which value should we use, and which ordering of processing and offset saving gives at-least-once consumption?
asks: project application.id
Which ordering of processing and offset saving gives at-least-once consumption?
turns.answer: The project application.id is oak-scale-17. Read, process, then save the position gives at-least-once consumption.
key_facts: The project application.id is oak-scale-17.
Read, process, then save the position gives at-least-once consumption.

evidence.quote: set application.id to oak-scale-17
| Read → process → save position | First messages are re-processed by the new owner | **At least once** |
